title: Runbook
description: An ordered checklist in which every step carries its own verify. Answers 'what is the correct way to do this' before starting. 2.0 (ADR-0019): a runbook is identified by its `uid` (a UUIDv7 created with it) and names its `type`; the numbered `id` (and the LL-NEW placeholder a hook used to allocate) is gone, and the number it is shown with is computed from its place among its siblings (`order`, then creation). 2.1 (additive): `lessons` names lessons by uid, as every record link does (ADR-0019); a 2.0 document's numbered `LL-NNN` codes still validate, so 2.0 stays readable, but a record holding one is refused by the record validation (homelabnext.registers.schema) and is migrated by `hnx records assign-uids`. 2.2 (additive, ADR-0032): an optional `summary`, one reviewed line of at most 160 characters, the level 0 that context_for serves.

uid.description: A canonical UUIDv7: the record's identity, never changed.

order.description: Optional sort key among its siblings.

summary.description: Optional (ADR-0032): the record's level 0, one reviewed line of at most 160 characters; context_for serves it instead of the content. The pattern refuses control characters (C0, DEL, C1) and the common invisible format characters (soft hyphen, U+061C, U+180E, zero-width and direction marks U+200B-U+200F, line and paragraph separators and bidi embeddings U+2028-U+202E, U+2060-U+206F, the BOM, U+FFF9-U+FFFB); `(?!\n)` keeps a validator whose `$` matches before a final newline (Python's) from accepting one. `hnx registers summaries` and the record validation are authoritative: they refuse every character of the Unicode categories Cc, Cf, Zl, Zp and Cs and surrounding whitespace, and count a record without a summary as a warning.

when.description: Trigger: when to open this runbook.

anyOf.description: 2.0: a numbered lesson code, before uids; readable, never written (a record holding one is refused).

lessons.description: 2.1: the lessons the runbook was written from, by uid (ADR-0019).

uid.description: A record uid: a canonical UUIDv7 (lowercase, version 7), created with the record and never changed (ADR-0019).
